text: Vindicate me, O God, and plead my case against a faithless nation; rescue me from the deceitful and unjust.
For you are God, my stronghold—why have you rejected me? Why must I go about in mourning, oppressed by the enemy?

versions.text: For you are the God of my refuge—why have you cast me off? Why must I go about in mourning, oppressed by the enemy?
versions.explanation: מָעוֹז means "stronghold/fortress," and the phrase is best read as "God of my strength" or "God, my stronghold"; "the God of my refuge" is slightly awkward and blurs the appositional force. "Rejected" also renders זנח a bit more precisely than "cast off" and reads smoothly aloud.

text: Send out your light and your truth; let them lead me. Let them bring me to your holy mountain, to your dwelling place.

versions.text: Send out your light and your truth; let them lead me. Let them bring me to your holy mountain, to the place where you dwell.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew noun (plural of מִשְׁכָּן) refers to God's dwelling place/tabernacle; "to your dwelling place" is tighter and more rhythmic for oral reading than the relative clause "the place where you dwell."

text: Then I will come to the altar of God, to God, my joy and my delight, and I will praise you with the harp, O God, my God.
Why are you cast down, my soul? Why so restless within me? Hope in God, for I will praise him again—the salvation of my face and my God.

versions.text: Why are you cast down, my soul? Why so restless within me? Hope in God, for I will praise him again—my salvation and my God.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "the salvation of my face/countenance," echoing the mourning imagery of verse 2 (going about with a darkened face). The current rendering drops "my face" entirely, losing the link between God's saving help and the lifting of the psalmist's downcast countenance.
